title: New-Hire Onboarding
description: The most important things to know in your first week — how Quiz Lab is built, shipped, and how work flows through Studio AI.

questions.prompt: Where do quiz pack JSON files live in the repo?
choices: static/quizzes/
src/packs/
app/src/lib/data/packs/
public/data/
questions.explanation: Pack files live in app/src/lib/data/packs/ — one JSON file per pack, picked up by the packs index (Architecture Overview; Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: What is the entire production deploy pipeline for Quiz Lab?
choices: Merge to main → GitHub Actions build → GitHub Pages
A manual release step run by the on-call engineer
Pushing a Docker image to a Vercel project
A nightly cron job that redeploys the database
questions.explanation: Merging to main triggers a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the static site and publishes it to GitHub Pages — there is no separate deploy or release step (Architecture Overview; Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: Which stack is Quiz Lab actually built on?
choices: Next.js on Vercel with a Postgres database
A React SPA backed by a REST API server
Plain HTML served from an Express backend
SvelteKit 2 + Vite with the static adapter — no server or database
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is a SvelteKit 2 app built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-static — fully prerendered, with no server runtime and no database; all content ships in the build (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: Under what base path is the app served on GitHub Pages?
choices: /quiz-lab
/product-demo
/app
questions.explanation: The site is served from GitHub Pages under the base path /product-demo (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: How does a change land on the main branch?
choices: Commit directly to main once the tests pass
Through a reviewed pull request that is squash-merged
By tagging a release and pushing the tag
Via a long-lived develop branch merged each month
questions.explanation: The team practices trunk-based development: you never commit directly to main — all work lands through a reviewed, squash-merged pull request (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: How many reviewer approvals does a PR need before it can merge?
choices: One
Zero — self-merge is fine
Two
Approval from every team member
questions.explanation: Every PR needs one reviewer approval before merge (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: What is the standard for new user-facing content such as a quiz pack?
choices: It can be AI-generated from any convenient source
It should match the claims in the marketing one-pager
It only needs to make the build pass
It must be grounded in a cited source document
questions.explanation: New user-facing content must be grounded in a cited source; explanations should be factual and reference the source, never invented (Engineering Handbook; Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: How many answer choices must each quiz question have?
choices: Exactly 4
Between 2 and 5
Any number
questions.explanation: The Pack Authoring Guide requires each question's choices array to contain exactly 4 options (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: What does a question's correctIndex field hold?
choices: The correct answer stored as a string
The 1-based position of the answer
An integer 0–3 that indexes into the choices array
A boolean marking whether the question is graded
questions.explanation: correctIndex is an integer from 0 to 3 that indexes into the four-element choices array (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: How many questions should a pack contain?
choices: Exactly 10
At least 20
No limit
questions.explanation: The style rules call for 10–15 questions per pack, with mixed difficulty (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: In Studio AI, what is the difference between an idea and a task?
choices: An idea is a hypothesis to validate; a task is one PR-sized piece of executing it
An idea is a bug report; a task is a feature request
They are two names for the same thing
An idea is the code; a task is the documentation
questions.explanation: An idea is a hypothesis you want to validate; a task is one discrete, PR-sized piece of executing it, linked to the idea (Engineering Handbook; Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: What happens when an agent picks up a task with work_on_next_task?
choices: It opens a pull request automatically
It deploys the current build to production
It merges the task's branch into main
It moves the task to inProgress and injects the task's curated context
questions.explanation: work_on_next_task moves the task to inProgress and injects its curated context — the attached documents — into the pickup response (Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: What makes a well-curated context 'neighborhood' for a task?
choices: Every document in the product's knowledge base
About 5 of the most relevant documents — the minimum the agent needs
Only the task specification, with no documents
A folder of source-code files from the repo
questions.explanation: A well-curated neighborhood is ~5 documents — the smallest set of the most relevant docs the agent needs and nothing else — delivered in one shot at pickup (Studio AI SDLC & MCP).
